data.description:
# Respect MunitoAI `x-ratelimit-*` reset headers on quota 429s

## Goal

The proxy currently treats MunitoAI quota 429s as generic per-account rate
limits: it applies only the standard short provider cooldown (60s +
exponential backoff) and discards the rate-limit reset information MunitoAI
exposes via its `x-ratelimit-*` response headers. Add reset-aware handling so
an exhausted MunitoAI account is skipped with an accurate cooldown/reset time
instead of being re-tried blindly inside the reset window — while siblings on
the same gateway with independent quota (e.g. paid `munitoai` vs
`munitoai-free`) remain eligible, preserving the per-request account-key
exclusion semantics of LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N.

## Scope carve-out vs LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (partial overlap)

- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** ("honour x-ratelimit-* headers when queuing 429
  cooldowns", **completed, merged as commit `1245f383` on dev**) owns the
  **generic header-parsing
  engine**: parsing `x-ratelimit-reset-requests/tokens/...` and
  `x-ratelimit-over-limit` into a cooldown, behind a per-provider
  `respect_ratelimit_headers` flag (default off). It also surfaces the
  resolved cooldown in `cooldown_seconds` and provider-state.json.
- **This item** owns the **account-scoped application** on top of that
  parsing: the reset-derived cooldown must poison **only the failing account
  key** (`api_key_env`) for the remainder of the request, leaving paid
  siblings on the same gateway eligible (LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N semantics), and
  must compose correctly with the chain-hold cycle. Header parsing is a
  **blocking dependency** (LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ) — do not re-implement it in
  this item; consume the shared parse path if already merged, otherwise land
  the parser within that item first.

## Context / findings

Investigation of a live "what happens on a quota error" question (2026-10-18)
established:

- **Observed MunitoAI 429 body** (35 occurrences in proxy.log on 2026-10-18):
  `{"error":{"message":"Too Many Requests","type":"rate_limit_error","param":null,"code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}`
  — no `Retry-After` header, no `"Resets in ..."` duration, no
  `metadata.limitName`.
- **MunitoAI signals rate-limit state via `x-ratelimit-*` headers** (live
  probe): `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests`,
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` (e.g. `"32s"`), `x-ratelimit-over-limit`.
  The proxy parses **none** of these headers (zero references in
  `proxy/proxy/*.py`).
- Because `_usage_limit_reset_info()` only recognises
  `GoUsageLimitError`/`FreeUsageLimitError` and `_parse_retry_after()` finds
  no header, `munitoai-free` gets only the standard 60s backoff cooldown and
  is re-tried every cycle — the observed logs show repeated
  `munitoai-free in cooldown (Ns remaining)` lines and fallback onto paid
  opencode/DeepSeek tiers.
- LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (completed, v0.1.22) already makes a plain
  `rate_limit_exceeded` 429 account-keyed for *per-request eligibility* via
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error` + `_usage_limit_account_key` poisoning the
  `attempted_domains` set; this item extends reset-awareness to the
  cooldown/quarantine duration itself, consistent with that infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Reset-aware cooldown:** when a 429 `rate_limit_error` response
      from a MunitoAI provider includes an `x-ratelimit-reset-*` header
      (or `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes` with a reset), the proxy applies the
      parsed reset duration (+ existing 2-minute safety margin) as the
      effective cooldown / quarantine for the failing account instead of the
      generic 60s backoff; a missing/zero reset value degrades to current
      behaviour.
- [ ] **AC2 — Account-scoped, sibling-preserving:** the reset-aware exclusion
      poisons only the failing account key (per `api_key_env`) for the rest
      of the request; paid siblings on the same gateway remain eligible —
      LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N semantics preserved.
- [ ] **AC3 — Fallback/chain-hold preserved:** a quota-429 account advances
      the chain to the next provider this request; chain-hold cycles
      (300s hold, max 3, 720s budget) still apply when all providers are
      exhausted.
- [ ] **AC4 — Unit tests:** (a) 429 + `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 32s` →
      accurate cooldown, account excluded inside the reset window; (b) 429
      without any reset signal → current short-cooldown + account-key
      poisoning behaviour unchanged; (c) no regression on the
      `FreeUsageLimitError` (3h cooldown) / `GoUsageLimitError`
      (quarantine) paths.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green** via `/skill:test` before `in_review`.

## Constraints

- Do not re-implement `x-ratelimit-*` header parsing — depends on the shared
  parse path from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ.
- Keep sibling-account eligibility unchanged (LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: `_parse_retry_after()` handles only
  `Retry-After`; `_usage_limit_reset_info()` recognises only
  `GoUsageLimitError`/`FreeUsageLimitError`; `_is_account_rate_limit_error()`
  and `_usage_limit_account_key()` (from LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) detect
  account-keyed 429s; the fallback loop applies `account_key`-scoped
  `attempted_domains` poisoning for quota 429s.

## Desired change

- On a quota 429 with a reset header, set the account's effective
  cooldown/quarantine to reset+margin (instead of 60s backoff), scoped to the
  failing `api_key_env` so siblings stay eligible; keep chain-hold and
  fallback semantics unchanged.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_parse_retry_after`, `_usage_limit_reset_info`,
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error`, `_usage_limit_account_key`, cooldown
  bookkeeping and fallback loop — apply and scope the reset-derived cooldown.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — provider chain entries `munitoai` / `munitoai-free`
  (per-provider flags consumed from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ).
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — account-key poisoning and
  sibling-eligibility tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` — reset-path no-regression tests.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** — "Proxy: honour MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* headers
  when queuing 429 cooldowns" (**completed, merged `1245f383`**) — previously
  a blocking dependency; the generic header-parsing engine now lives in this
  codebase and is consumed, not re-implemented.
- **LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N** — "Paid MunitoAI tier is skipped ... when the free
  tier hits a per-account 429" (completed, v0.1.22) — account-key eligibility
  foundation this item builds on.
- **LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL** — "Do not over-use MinutoAI-free" (completed) —
  free-tier request-budget gate; adjacent quota management.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (duplicate-check, 2026-10-18): "LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (Intake Complete,
  in-flight) already scopes honouring `x-ratelimit-*` headers for 429
  cooldowns — is this item a duplicate?" — Answer (Map): "Partial overlap,
  not a duplicate. LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ owns generic header parsing +
  provider-level cooldown; this item owns account-scoped application with
  sibling preservation (per LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) and chain-hold interplay.
  Rewritten to carve out the delta; blocking dependency recorded." Source:
  `wl search munitoai ratelimit reset` + AC comparison of both items; comment
  added to LP-0MVDNP36J006430L.

- OPEN QUESTION (RESOLVED at plan, 2026-10-19): sequencing — header parsing
  lives in LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ, which was in-flight. — Answer (Map): resolved
  with evidence — LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ is **completed** (stage in_review) and
  merged into `dev` as commit `1245f383`; the parser helpers
  (`_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `_ratelimit_over_limit`,
  `_get_respect_ratelimit_headers`, `_parse_ratelimit_duration`) are present
  in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` and `munitoai` / `munitoai-free` both set
  `respect_ratelimit_headers: true` in `proxy/config.yaml`. No further
  blocking; this item layers the account-scoped quarantine on top. Evidence:
  `wl show LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ --json` (status completed, stage in_review),
  `git log --oneline -15` showing `1245f383 LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ: Implementation complete`.


## Plan (decomposition, 2026-10-19)

Test-first feature decomposition of the account-scoped application; each
feature is a minimal end-to-end slice. Dependency chain: tests → implement →
docs.

1. **LP-0MVFA0PAV0022ZHO — Tests: reset-aware account quarantine (test-first)**
   — red tests for the account-scoped quarantine, sibling preservation,
   chain-hold/Retry-After, degrade path, flag gate, and Go/Free no-regression.
2. **LP-0MVFA1VRT007T9HT — Implement reset-derived account quarantine** —
   account-keyed `_usage_reset_at` quarantine (reset + 120 s margin) applied
   from the shared `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown` primitive, consumed by
   the existing exclusion and Retry-After machinery unchanged.
3. **LP-0MVFA2A0Z004PW3N — Docs: reset-aware account quarantine** — update
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` comments, `proxy/README.md`.

Design decisions (grounded in the AC text and the merged code, no new knobs):

- The reset-derived cooldown is routed through the EXISTING account-quarantine
  path (`_set_usage_limit_quarantine` + `_UsageLimitReset(explicit=True)`),
  which adds the existing **2-minute safety margin**
  (`_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` = 120) named in AC1 — distinct from the
  **2-second** `ratelimit_cooldown_margin_seconds` applied to the
  provider-entry cooldown by LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ.
- Account key = `_usage_limit_account_key(provider_cfg)` (`api_key_env`@
  endpoint:model), so paid siblings with a different `api_key_env` are never
  quarantined; the per-request `attempted_domains` poisoning from
  LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N is unchanged.
- AC1's "instead of the generic 60s backoff" is satisfied by the existing
  `max(exponential backoff, reset + margin)` interplay: the account quarantine
  is the authoritative, persisted record of the upstream reset and feeds
  `_compute_retry_after()` and chain-hold unchanged.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19T13:25 — plan session: decomposed into 3 children
  (LP-0MVFA0PAV0022ZHO, LP-0MVFA1VRT007T9HT, LP-0MVFA2A0Z004PW3N), wired
  test-first dependency edges, ran the six automated review stages + AC
  coverage review (100% parent-AC coverage), refreshed effort/risk estimates
  (parent Small/Medium, E≈6.7h). Session: herdr-1792414357-3987593-12728.

## Goal

Pin the off-peak-windowed, all-opencode low-priority fallback behaviour with tests **before** the config change (test-first).

## Scope

Tests only; no production behaviour change in this item.

## Work

1. **Window gating:** an `available_times`-carrying entry is skipped outside its UTC window (`_is_within_allowed_window` → `Skipping provider=...: outside its available_times window (UTC)`) and selected inside it.
2. **Chain order:** `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code resolves to `local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`. (Red until the config item lands — intended TDD state; document the convention if the repo requires green main.)
3. **Per-key 429 failover (the key behaviour):** a 429 from `opencode-go-3` must NOT exclude `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` from the same request — rate-limit quarantine is keyed on `_usage_limit_account_key` (`api_key_env@endpoint`), so sibling accounts are independent (LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
4. **Same-domain 5xx caveat:** a 5xx from `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude its same-gateway siblings as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) — assert the honest behaviour so nobody assumes 3× outage resilience.
5. **No paid-tier leak:** `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in any `low` chain.
6. **Medium/high unaffected:** those chains are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests cover in-window selection, out-of-window skip-and-fall-through, and behaviour-neutrality when the free tier still has budget.
2. A test asserts the exact 5-entry low chain order for plan, author and code.
3. A test asserts 429-per-account failover lets sibling opencode keys be tried in the same request.
4. A test asserts 5xx does NOT give sibling failover (same failure domain).
5. A test asserts `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` absent from `low` chains and `medium`/`high` chains unchanged.
6. Reuses existing proxy test conventions (monkeypatched clock for `available_times`, existing timing-gate fixtures) rather than inventing new harness code.
7. full suite green via `/skill:test`, except the documented intentional red chain-order assertion pending the config item.

data.description:
## Goal

Let `low`-priority requests fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible `available_times` windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the 2-rpm free tier.

## Operator decisions

- **Do not widen any `available_times`** — the existing off-peak windows are the paid-spend boundary and stay byte-identical.
- **Allow all opencode models** on the low chain, not just one entry.

## Background (measured)

- `low` chain today (plan/author/code): `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]`, with `munitoai-free` at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and last in the chain → overflow has nowhere to go but an upstream 429.
- Three opencode entries per model, same gateway/model, each with its own key: `opencode-go-3` (`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`), `opencode-go-2` (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`), `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`), all with `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`.
- Window-closed entries are skipped with `continue` (`provider.py`, ~line 2079), so appending them after `munitoai-free` is behaviour-neutral outside the windows.
- **429 failover is per API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`; LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) → the three entries give genuine 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **5xx/stall is per failure domain** (`_failure_domain_key`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) → siblings are skipped as one domain during an outage; not 3× resilience. Document this.
- **UTC/local overlap:** `available_times` are UTC; the cheap window (local `Europe/Dublin` 01:00–10:00) = UTC 00:00–09:00; opencode unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 → ~3 of 9 cheap hours gain capacity. Accepted.

## Work

1. Set `priority_routes.low` for `plan`, `author`, `code` in `proxy/config.yaml` to:
   `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`
   (free tier still preferred before any paid entry; the three opencode keys ordered as they appear in the `providers` lists so cache affinity matches the medium/high hot path).
2. Change **no** `available_times` value anywhere in the file.
3. Update the `priority_routes` block comment: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 rationale, and the same-domain-5xx caveat.
4. Update `priority.py::priority_routing_profile`'s docstring if/where it asserts "low never spends on paid tiers" so it states the off-peak-gated exception.
5. Leave `medium`/`high` chains, `compact`, `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` untouched.

## Key files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `models.plan/author/code.priority_routes.low` + comments
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `priority_routing_profile` docstring
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference for `_is_within_allowed_window`, `_usage_limit_account_key`, `_failure_domain_key`

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code is exactly `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. `git diff proxy/config.yaml` contains **zero** changed `available_times` lines.
3. `medium` and `high` chains are byte-identical to before; `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` appear in no `low` chain.
4. Outside the windows the resolution order and behaviour are identical to today (proved by the test item).
5. `proxy/config.yaml` parses via `yaml.safe_load`; full suite passes via `/skill:test`.
6. Comments/docstring record all four rationale points (off-peak exception, 3-of-9 overlap, per-key-429 capacity, same-domain-5xx caveat).

# Implement reset-derived account quarantine

## Goal

As a proxy operator, I want a MunitoAI quota 429 that advertises its reset
window to quarantine the failing API-key ACCOUNT for that window, so the free
tier is not re-probed every cycle while paid siblings on the same gateway stay
eligible.

## Scope

Production code only, driven by the red tests from the test-first sibling
item. One change site: the shared HTTP-error primitive
`_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`, which both fallback loops already call.

## Design

- Reuse the merged parsing engine from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ
  (`_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `_ratelimit_over_limit`,
  `_get_respect_ratelimit_headers`) — do not parse headers again.
- When the response is a **quota 429** (HTTP 429 AND
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error(response, body_text)` OR
  `_ratelimit_over_limit(response.headers)`) AND the entry opts in via
  `respect_ratelimit_headers` AND a reset duration parses, record an
  account-scoped quarantine:
  `_set_usage_limit_quarantine(_usage_limit_account_key(provider_cfg),
  _UsageLimitReset(reset + _USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS, True, label))`.
  `explicit=True` keeps it persisted to `provider-state.json` and exempt from
  the guessed-quarantine 24 h cap.
- The account key (`api_key_env@endpoint:model`, see
  `_usage_limit_account_key`) is what `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`
  already consults via `_usage_reset_remaining`, so sibling preservation and
  cross-request skipping come for free with no change to `attempted_domains`
  semantics.
- Keep the existing provider-ENTRY cooldown / exponential backoff and the
  `Retry-After` precedence untouched; the account quarantine is additive and
  is the authoritative record of the upstream reset.
- Add a small private helper (for example
  `_apply_ratelimit_account_quarantine`) next to the existing
  `_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds` helpers, which decides whether the response
  is a quota 429 and applies the quarantine, returning the applied reset (or
  `None`) for the attempt record. Call it from
  `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown` where `ratelimit_reset` is already
  computed, immediately before `mark_provider_unavailable` — one site covers
  both fallback loops.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Reset-aware cooldown: when a 429 rate_limit_error response includes an x-ratelimit-reset-* header, the account quarantine is the parsed reset plus the 2-minute margin.
- [ ] AC2 — Account-scoped, sibling-preserving: the reset-aware exclusion poisons only the failing account key, so paid siblings stay eligible.
- [ ] AC3 — Fallback/chain-hold preserved: a quota-429 account advances the chain, and chain-hold cycles still apply when every provider is exhausted.
- [ ] AC4 — Degrade path: a missing, zero or unparseable reset applies the current behaviour with no account quarantine.
- [ ] AC5 — No regression: the FreeUsageLimitError 3h cooldown and GoUsageLimitError quarantine paths are untouched.
- [ ] AC6 — Observability: the attempt record carries cooldown_seconds, ratelimit_reset_seconds and ratelimit_over_limit plus an account-quarantine marker.
- [ ] AC7 — Full suite green via /skill:test before in_review, including the changed-scope gate.

## Behaviour detail

- The attempt record for the reset path carries the existing fields
  (`cooldown_seconds`, `ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `ratelimit_over_limit`) plus
  a marker that an account quarantine was applied, so the behaviour is
  observable in diagnostics.
- The provider-entry cooldown line stays unchanged so the existing
  `Skipping provider=… in cooldown` diagnostics and
  `test_ratelimit_headers_cooldown.py` assertions still hold.
- Chain-hold semantics are preserved because `_compute_retry_after()` already
  scans `_usage_reset_at`: an all-exhausted chain holds (300 s, max 3 cycles,
  720 s budget) when the quarantine fits the budget, or returns the
  exhaustion response immediately with the quarantine-derived `retry_after`
  when it does not.

## Constraints

- No new config knobs: reuse `respect_ratelimit_headers`,
  `ratelimit_cooldown_margin_seconds` and the existing 120 s usage-limit
  margin constant.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` only — no changes to routing config, budgets or
  the budget gate.
- Do not change `_compute_retry_after`, `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`
  or the chain-hold helpers; the new quarantine must be consumed by them
  as-is.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`, the x-ratelimit-* helper block, `_set_usage_limit_quarantine`, `_usage_limit_account_key`, `_is_account_rate_limit_error`.
- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` — the red tests this change must turn green.
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — sibling-eligibility and per-request exclusion assertions.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test-first sibling item (red tests must exist first).

## Deliverables

- Implemented behaviour in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- Green changed-scope test gate; commit recorded on this work item.

# Docs: reset-aware account quarantine

## Goal

As a proxy operator reading the repository docs, I want the reset-aware,
account-scoped 429 quarantine documented next to the existing cooldown and
usage-limit-quarantine descriptions, so the two distinct safety margins and
the sibling-preservation guarantee are discoverable without reading
`provider.py`.

## Scope

Documentation and configuration comments only — no behavioural change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — routing.md documents the account-scoped quarantine: which 429 body and header signals trigger it, the parsed reset plus the 2-minute usage-limit margin versus the 2-second ratelimit_cooldown_margin_seconds.
- [ ] AC2 — routing.md states the account key (api_key_env@endpoint:model) and that paid siblings on the same gateway stay eligible.
- [ ] AC3 — routing.md states the consequences: persistence in provider-state.json, the exhaustion retry_after, and chain-hold interplay.
- [ ] AC4 — The respect_ratelimit_headers comment blocks in config.yaml (per-entry and server.*) mention the account quarantine and both margins.
- [ ] AC5 — The provider-fallback cooldown list in README.md gains a bullet for the reset-aware account quarantine, adjacent to the usage-limit quarantine bullet.
- [ ] AC6 — Documented behaviour matches the merged implementation exactly, with no invented knobs.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the existing "Upstream rate-limit headers" section in
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` with one `####` account-scoped subsection (bullet
  list only).
- Add two to three comment lines to each of the two `respect_ratelimit_headers`
  blocks in `proxy/config.yaml`.
- Add one bullet to the cooldown list in `proxy/README.md`.

## Constraints

- UK English; match the surrounding prose style and bullet format.
- No new configuration keys; document only what exists.
- Do not restate the LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ parsing rules in full — link by
  reference instead.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — canonical behaviour reference for rate-limit headers and cooldowns.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — operator-facing documentation of the provider entry and server flags.
- `proxy/README.md` — provider-fallback cooldown and quarantine summary list.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only verification of documented behaviour.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the implementation item (docs must describe merged behaviour).

## Deliverables

- Updated docs and config comments.
- Commit recorded on this work item.
